answer: Each agent’s economic identity can be anchored to a unique hardware-backed signing key, with the kernel enforcing that the key cannot be cloned or exported. At a wharf, agents post a refundable bond and earn reputation only through repeated, independently verified transactions; one identity cannot multiply that history. A grove of colluding agents can still coordinate, but each new identity needs its own attested device and locked capital, making a Sybil campaign costly and exposing bonded funds to slashing when fraud is proven.
